summary: Iteration 9 tested the light Chrome redesign, the live screencast WebSocket and the resizable/collapsible layout on the cloud target. Backend: the new tests/test_iter9_stream.py passes 5 of 7, and the iter7 regression passes 6 of 6. Streaming: an animated page streams at 60 fps. Resize is applied and clamped to 640-2560 x 400-1600 (both 1000x700 and the out-of-range values were checked), and bad resize values are ignored without breaking the stream. The stream follows tab new/switch/close. Click, dblclick, type, key (Enter), scroll and move all drive the page, an unknown kind returns a JSON error, and an unknown group returns {type:error}. A 'move' during a running task leaves it running, while a 'click' pauses it (take over). The two failures are because an invalid token or bad group is refused at the HTTP handshake with 403, not closed with 4401/4400. UI: the sign-in page is light. The live indicator is green with the title 'Live stream'. browser-screen and browser-frame-image both have computed cursor 'default'. The tab strip is #DEE1E6 with a white active tab and favicons, and the omnibox has a lock icon on https. Typing into the Wikipedia search box shows suggestions in about 1 second, and wheel scrolling scrolls the remote page. Every side panel (all 9) and the workspace, template and skill-review dialogs are white with dark text; no dark leftovers were found by a computed-style scan. Layout: toggle-left/right, the collapse buttons inside the panels, rail click (the active icon collapses, another icon expands), and dragging the left and right handles all work. Sizes are kept after reload through localStorage 'react-resizable-panels:shadow-layout'. toggle-workspace-bar hides the bar and is remembered. After any panel change the remote page re-renders at the new screen size (nat == screen). Regression passed: workspace create, switch, grid, solo pop-out (/?group=..&solo=1 has no rail or left toggle and shows the workspace label), tabs new/switch/close, omnibox navigation, back/reload, Watch me to the skill-review dialog (discarded; 'move' events are not recorded), and a command run that finished with 'The page title is: Example Domain'. MAIN BUG: on first load the frame is often letterboxed with the wrong aspect ratio. Examples: viewport 1058x821 but frames 1058x661 or 1058x473. The stale frame stays until a panel is resized, and the click y-mapping is wrong while it lasts.

minor.issue: Invalid token and bad group call ws.close(4401/4400) BEFORE ws.accept(), so Starlette rejects the handshake with HTTP 403 and clients never receive close codes 4401/4400 (browser sees 1006). Rejection itself works. Fix: await ws.accept() first, then ws.close(code=4401/4400), if the codes matter (e.g. so the frontend stops retrying on auth failure).

Stale or wrong-size screencast after connect. Repro on Main/wikipedia (run python /app/tests/iter9_main_probe.py): GET /browser/state shows viewport 1058x821, the first frame (page.screenshot) is 1058x821 but cropped from a 1280-wide layout, and all later screencast frames are 1058x661 (the old 1280x800 aspect). In the UI right after login, frame-image naturalWidth/Height were 1058x661 or 1058x473 (the 473 matches the previous session's 1838x821 viewport) while browser-screen was 1058x821, giving grey bars top and bottom. It fixes itself as soon as any real viewport change happens (panel toggle). Likely race: set_viewport sets self.viewport before awaiting page.set_viewport_size, the stream loop restarts the screencast on the old layout, and a static page sends no more frames; it also early-returns when the viewport is unchanged even though the page layout isn't. Fix idea: set self.viewport only after set_viewport_size finishes, then restart the screencast (or send a fresh screenshot after resize), and always apply set_viewport_size on a new stream connection.

ui_bugs.issue: Click/scroll coordinates are mapped with state.viewport (w,h) over the img rect. When the frame's aspect differs from the viewport (the stale-frame case above), clicks land in the wrong place (y off by up to ~24-40%). Map using imgRef.naturalWidth/naturalHeight or the screencast metadata (deviceWidth/deviceHeight), or fix the backend race.
toggle-workspace-bar still shows in the solo pop-out but has no visible effect there, because SOLO never renders GroupBar.

action_items: Fix the stale or wrong-aspect screencast on initial connect: apply the viewport after set_viewport_size finishes, and restart the screencast or send a fresh frame once the resize has really taken effect. Repro: python /app/tests/iter9_main_probe.py
Map clicks using the frame's natural size or the screencast metadata instead of state.viewport
Optional: accept the WebSocket before closing with 4401/4400 so the close codes reach the client
Optional: hide toggle-workspace-bar in solo mode; replace the native date input and select with shadcn components; remove hover:border-slate-600
critical_code_review_comments: Group.set_viewport assigns self.viewport before the page resize finishes, so the stream loop races it (see the stale-frame bug)
The viewport is per group and shared, so two viewers of the same group (e.g. the main window plus a solo pop-out of the same group) will keep resizing each other's remote page
useLiveView falls back to polling after 2 failed connects, but on an auth failure (403 handshake) it keeps retrying the WS forever with backoff; acceptable, but a 4401 close would let it stop

stream(): on_frame is scheduled with ensure_future without backpressure; acks are sent after send, which is good, but a slow client can still queue tasks. Consider dropping frames while a send is pending

success_rate.backend: 71% iter9 (5/7; both failures are close-code semantics) + iter7 regression 100%
success_rate.frontend: ~92% (all flows pass; the initial letterboxed frame and click mapping are off)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && pytest tests/test_iter9_stream.py -n 0 -v -s (about 50s). The stale-frame check is python /app/tests/iter9_main_probe.py; it should print only frames matching the viewport size, e.g. (1058,821), with no (1058,661). In UI tests, compare browser-frame-image naturalWidth/Height with browser-screen right after login. Every browser_automation session starts with fresh localStorage, so layout persistence can only be checked with a reload inside one session. Do not use '%' in data: URLs (it breaks JS); a CSS animation page is the reliable fps source. The browser automation can read /tmp/tk.txt for a fresh ticket.
rca of the issue: Stale frame: Group.set_viewport sets self.viewport first and then awaits p.set_viewport_size. Group.stream polls every 0.25s, sees the key change, takes a screenshot and starts the screencast before Chrome has relaid out the page. Static pages send no more screencast frames, so the client keeps the wrong-aspect frame. If the stored viewport already equals the requested size, set_viewport returns early even when the page layout isn't at that size, which was seen on the Main wikipedia tab. Mitigation: apply set_viewport_size first, then update self.viewport (or bump a generation counter) so the stream restarts afterwards; re-send a page.screenshot after the resize; and on a new stream connection always force set_viewport_size.
